5658.t: Probably an Anatolian loanword; compare Luwian [script needed] (tuwarsa, “vine”).

5646.t: Traditionally derived from a Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₂w- (whence θεάομαι (theáomai), θῆβος (thêbos), θήγεια (thḗgeia)), an extension of *dʰeh₂-, with no clear cognates outside Hellenic; other extensions include θάμβος (thámbos) (< *dʰh₂n̥bʰos), τάφος…

5666.t: From καινός (kainós, “new”) + -της (-tēs, suffix forming nouns of state).

5661.t: From κατά (kătắ) + ἱζάνω (hĭzắnō, “to cause to sit”) with apocopic form καθ’.

5652.t: According to Beekes, possibly from the same Pre-Greek root of θώς (thṓs, “jackal”) and θῶσθαι (thôsthai, “to eat”).

5645.t: From the stem of τίθημι (títhēmi, “to place”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁-, possibly combined with the stem of ἵστημι (hístēmi, “to stand”), from Proto-Indo-European *steh₂-.

5696.t: From κατα- (kătă-, denoting motion downwards) + λέγω (légō, “to choose, to say”).

5610.t: From Proto-Hellenic *wéikō, from Proto-Indo-European *weyk- (“to curve, bend; exchange”).

5624.t: From εὐ- (eu-) + a derivative of ἵστημι (hĭ́stēmĭ, “to stand”).

5656.t: From Proto-Indo-European *dʰrew-, the same root of θρέομαι (thréomai, “to shriek, proclaim”) and Old Armenian երդնում (erdnum, “to swear, take an oath”).

5637.t: From εὐ- (eu-, “well, good”) + τάσσω (tássō, “draw up in order of battle, form, array, marshal”) + -τος (-tos, adjectival suffix).

5635.t: From κόπτω (kóptō, “to beat, strike, cut”), possibly with the semantics being "easy to hit."

5611.t: From Proto-Indo-European *welH- (“to turn, wind; to press together”).

5617.t: From εὐ- (eu-, “well-”) + λαβεῖν (labeîn, “to take hold of”) + -ης (-ēs, adjectival suffix).

5615.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₁su-ḱlewēs (“famous”) (compare Avestan *𐬵𐬎𐬯𐬭𐬀𐬎𐬎𐬀𐬵 (*husrauuah), Vedic Sanskrit सु॒श्रव॑स् (suśrávas). By surface analysis, εὐ- (eu-) + -κλεής (-kleḗs).
